resources.string: Off by default. Requires one enabled built-in or external ReZygisk, NeoZygisk or Zygisk Next provider; every change takes effect after a full reboot.
No enabled Zygisk provider was detected. Sui cannot be enabled.
The Zygisk setup has pending changes. Fully reboot before enabling Sui.
Multiple Zygisk providers are enabled or staged. Keep only one and fully reboot.
The Zygisk prerequisite could not be verified. Sui cannot be enabled; use a matching updated ksud and refresh.

Enable built-in Zygisk in Settings, or install and enable an external ReZygisk, NeoZygisk or Zygisk Next module, then fully reboot and refresh. External providers do not need to be installed by LunexSU. This dialog does not enable Zygisk or Sui. Detection is a prerequisite check, not proof of successful injection.
The bundled Sui payload is unavailable
Sui permissions are separate from kernel Root permissions.

Disabling requests the broker to stop. A full reboot is required to remove injection and end privileges or user services already running. Updating Manager does not automatically replace an installed Sui module.

Requires one enabled built-in or external ReZygisk, NeoZygisk or Zygisk Next provider and a full reboot. SystemUI and Settings must not be excluded from injection. This does not enable ZNN or ADB Root. Keep a working recovery path. Sui has its own privileged permission database.
Enabled but the Sui service is unavailable
UI simulation only. Refresh simulates a completed reboot; no real Sui service runs.

Apps request permission through Sui\'s own dialog in SystemUI; the Manager does not need to be open. Requests are denied while SystemUI is excluded from injection. Enabling Sui does not automatically grant apps access.
Changes apply to every package sharing this UID. Revoking Sui permissions does not change kernel Root grants.
Sui command outcome is unconfirmed. It may still finish; do not reboot until status is verified. New changes are blocked while checking.
Sui IPC timed out; the connection was reset. Refresh to verify any permission change before retrying.
